title: Planning Ahead: szeretném, ha and azért, hogy Together

sections.title: Five lessons, one plan
sections.content: You now have the whole toolkit for talking about an ambition: naming what you wish would happen (*szeretném, ha* / *bárcsak* + conditional), saying what you want to happen (*hogy* + -jon/-jen after *akar*/*szeretné*), and explaining the purpose behind your actions, positive or negative (*azért, hogy* / *nehogy* + -jon/-jen). A real plan usually needs more than one of these in the same breath: *szeretném, ha* names the outcome you're hoping for, *azért, hogy* explains the steps you're taking to reach it. *annak érdekében, hogy* ("for the purpose of, in the interest of") is a more formal, more written synonym of *azért, hogy* — useful when a five-year plan needs to sound serious and considered.

sections.title: Everyday vs. formal purpose
rows: for the purpose of, in the interest of (formal)

items.spanish: Szeretném, ha öt éven belül sikerülne saját vállalkozást indítanom, ezért mindent megteszek azért, hogy ez megvalósuljon.
items.english: I wish that within five years I could start my own business, so I'm doing everything so that this comes true.

items.spanish: Minden hónapban félreteszek egy kis pénzt, annak érdekében, hogy megvalósuljon a jövőképem.
items.english: I set aside a little money every month, for the purpose of making my vision for the future come true.

sections.content: *ezért* ("therefore") and *azért, hogy* ("so that") look similar but aren't interchangeable: *ezért* links two separate sentences by pointing back at a reason already given, while *azért, hogy* opens a brand-new purpose clause inside the same sentence, with its own -jon/-jen verb.
